operation: ExpandBar: expand the first item (layout from item 0)
method: the client rectangle read once per layout, a scratch RECT in ExpandItem.redraw: 2 x 10^5 GetClientRect calls -> 1, allocated 12815552 -> 15616 B per expand; height change 93876 -> 56962 us; 10^4: alloc 1283624 -> 3688 B (wall time within load noise)

operation: ExpandBar: scroll a page (WM_VSCROLL SB_PAGEDOWN, then the paint)
method: paint visits only the damaged run of items: binary search of its first item, stop below the damage (O(n) -> O(log n + window) per paint); append one item 12797 -> 3464 us; 10^4: scroll 4529 -> 2103 us, append 2211 -> 1904 us; before = O1 jar

operation: ExpandBar: mouse move over the headers (WM_MOUSEMOVE hover tracking)
unit: us per move (median of 5 x 100 moves, wall)
method: hover found by binary search (the last header starting above the point) and the hovered item tracked, so a move updates the old and the new item; WM_LBUTTONDOWN and WM_MOUSELEAVE without a scan; 10^4: 478 -> 61 us per move; before = O2 jar

operation: CTabFolder: select a far tab (folder update: setItemSize)
method: the close button size measured once per update instead of once per tab, the minimum widths in an array the folder keeps: allocated 6201472 -> 201272 B per select; rename 44054 -> 17512 us, resize 238345 -> 14787 us, append 130522 -> 20584 us (6099872 -> 99432 B); 10^4: select 89260 -> 28860 us

operation: OS light/dark switch (FlatLaf #204): M3LookAndFeel.update over the installed delegates
unit: us (median of 5, wall; the switch without the paint)
method: each widget class resolves its target look and feel once per switch (IdentityHashMap memo) instead of two property names and three property reads per widget: allocated 641640 -> 2080 B; 1000 delegates 24053 -> 4398 us; layouts per switch 0 (a cheap repaint: no metric key differs between light and dark); the paint that follows is the OS painting every child window (0.6 s at 1000, 3.6-4.1 s at 5000 native child windows), measured, not changed: drawn rows in one window are the scalable path

the bare line feeds counted first (none: the input itself), then one exact-size builder fed with the runs between them, no substring per line; wall 267954 -> 251197 us (the rest is the EDIT control and the TCHAR copy); 10^5 lines 12425688 -> 4755864 B, 49223 -> 32355 us; result proven equal to the stock conversion (Test_org_eclipse_swt_widgets_Display_WithCrLf, 20000 seeded strings)
catalogue_id: two-pass counting + exact-size buffer (no per-run allocation)

operation: ToolBar: append one item / rename a middle item
method: measured NO: 2 x 10^3 -> 10^4 items append 4.2 -> 16.0 ms, rename 3.5 -> 14.1 ms; a JFR profile puts 668 of about 800 samples in the toolbar window procedure (comctl32 relays out every button on TB_INSERTBUTTON and on the WM_SETFONT that ToolItem.setText sends) and about 130 in SWT (layoutItems text/image scans, setDropDownItems, resizeControl loops); counters for the scans (leaf B1) would remove at most the SWT share; the native relayout belongs to a drawn ToolBar (render modes)

operation: Synchronizer: bytes allocated per asyncExec on the posting thread
method: the ConcurrentLinkedQueue of RunnableLock replaced by a ring of slots per priority class (DispatchQueue): no RunnableLock and no queue node per call; syncExec reuses one lock per thread (brief rule 28)

operation: Synchronizer: throughput of 10^6 asyncExec from 4 threads drained by the UI thread
method: the same ring under one monitor per post and per poll, no queue nodes to allocate or collect

operation: Synchronizer: latency of one runnable posted behind a flood of 10^6
unit: us (median of 5; before: plain, the only class; after: the INPUT class)
method: priority classes (input, layout, default, model, idle): an INPUT runnable runs before the queued default ones; a plain one behind the flood still waits 104314 us (first in, first out, as stock)

operation: ExpandBar: WM_SETCURSOR with no header hovered (sent before every mouse move)
method: the hand cursor decided from the hovered item O4 tracks instead of a scan of every item; with a header hovered the scan stopped early (5381 -> 926 us); the paint run and the hover tests reduced to their invariants (coverage); Test_..._ExpandBar_Hover 4/4 in the viewport and the original mode
catalogue_id: tracked state (delta) instead of a scan

operation: CTabFolder: one mouse move over the tabs
method: setItemLocation records the showing tabs (left to right in index order); the tab under the mouse is a binary search and only the tab under it, the tab it left and the selected tab change state (every other tab is at rest); mouse down, up and exit use the same search; stale indexes (a tab created, disposed or reordered before the layout) fall back to the stock scan; 10^4: 995 -> 29 us. Proof: Test_..._CTabFolder_Hover, the stock CTabFolder and CTabItem suites and the differential against a fresh official recording, 147/0 in the viewport and the original mode
